scope: Frontend behavior per tab after the two-tab race resolves: what each tab does, cookie clearing, Tab A token usability

evidence.observation: When Tab B's refreshSession() returns false (the /auth/refresh POST returned 401), the very next statement is logout(). No error message, no recovery attempt.
logout() redirects Tab B's browser to /login immediately. The rt cookie is already cleared server-side (httpOnly, inaccessible to JS). Tab B lands on login with no error shown.

Tab A's refreshSession() returned true (it got 200). Tab A retries the original API call with the new access token. But the new access token's fid embeds the now-revoked family_id. The retry hits authMiddleware which calls isFamilyRevoked(fid) and returns 401.

evidence.quote:
if (!retry.ok) throw new Error(`Request failed: ${retry.status}`);
    return retry.json() as Promise<T>;
evidence.observation: When the retry returns 401 (because isFamilyRevoked rejects the new token), api() throws 'Request failed: 401'. There is no second refresh attempt and no logout() call from this code path. The thrown error propagates to Dashboard.useEffect.

Promise.all has no .catch(). If any api() call throws (e.g. Tab A's retry returns 401 due to revoked family), the error is an unhandled promise rejection. Dashboard shows nothing — the user sees a blank page, not a login redirect.

hypotheses.statement: Tab B is logged out silently: refreshSession() returns false → logout() → /login, with no error message. The rt cookie was already cleared server-side, invisible to JS.

Tab A receives a 200 from /auth/refresh and a new access token, but the new token's fid points to a revoked family. Tab A's retry of the original API call gets 401 from authMiddleware. api() throws 'Request failed: 401' without calling logout().

Tab A's Dashboard shows a blank/stale UI (unhandled rejection from Promise.all). Tab A is not redirected to /login by this code path, but every subsequent API call will also fail with 401 because the family is revoked. The user sees broken UI rather than a login redirect — a second symptom of the same bug.
Client-side deduplication of refreshSession() cannot fix the two-tab bug. Each tab is an independent JS context with its own module state. A shared in-flight promise only works within one tab.
